stock: 255/75R17 (Sport S, Sahara and most special editions)

wheel.lug_torque: 100 lb-ft (Northridge4x4); ExtremeTerrain gives an 85–125 lb-ft range [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]

max_tire.note: JEGS puts the stock-height limit at about 33 in. Driving Line fitted 35x12.50R17s to a stock-height 2017 JK Unlimited Sport on 4.75 in-backspacing wheels after removing the front splash guard, and concluded that real off-road use needs aftermarket or heavily trimmed flares.
285/75R17 works on factory 17s; 35x12.50 wants 18x9 or 20x9 wheels at about 0 to +1 mm offset.
JEGS says 37s need about 3.5 in of lift and advises axle, driveshaft and gearing upgrades; 40s need about 4.5 in.

items.title: Driver airbag clockspring
items.summary: Dust can contaminate the clockspring so the driver's airbag may not deploy; Chrysler recall S33, 388,532 vehicles.

items.title: Takata passenger airbag inflator
items.summary: Passenger airbag inflator may rupture as the propellant degrades; this campaign covered trucks sold or registered in hot, humid states.

items.title: Takata passenger inflator (Zone A states)
items.summary: Passenger inflator replacement for trucks sold or registered in hot, humid states (recall U03).

items.title: Driver airbag inflator
items.summary: Driver inflator may over-pressurise and explode on deployment (recall V01).

items.title: Automatic transmission overheat warning
items.summary: Autos lacked a fluid-temperature warning; fluid could boil over onto hot parts. Dealers add a 'HOT OIL' message and chime (recall J30).

items.title: Front brake lines vs inner fender liner
items.summary: Inner fender liners can rub through front brake hoses and cause a leak (recall K13).

items.title: Axle-to-chassis fastener torque
items.summary: Front and rear axle attachment fasteners could lose torque; dealers re-torque all 19 (recall L09).

items.title: Power-steering line rubs transmission cooler tube
items.summary: 3.6 automatics: the power-steering return line can wear a hole in the transmission cooler tube (recall N28, 180,131 vehicles).

items.title: Heated mirror connector short
items.summary: Corrosion in the heated power-mirror connector can short.

items.title: Front impact sensor wiring
items.summary: Sensor wiring can pull loose in some crashes before it signals the airbags.

items.title: Right-hand-drive airbag clockspring
items.summary: Right-hand-drive (postal) trucks built February 2010 to May 2016: dust can contaminate the clockspring and disable the driver's airbag. See also 11V-528 and 13V-176 (2008–2012 RHD) and 24V-196 (2016 RHD).

tsbs.title: Death wobble: Chrysler steering-vibration bulletin
tsbs.summary: In August 2012 Chrysler sent dealers a bulletin acknowledging the solid-axle shimmy, naming aftermarket parts, wrong tire pressures and worn steering and suspension components as causes. NHTSA had earlier concluded the condition doesn't cause loss of control.

tsbs.title: Shimmy with the 4-inch Mopar lift
tsbs.summary: 2012–2015 JKs built before June 15, 2015 with the Mopar 4 in lift: replace the front axle track bar bracket and recheck alignment (supersedes 02-008-15).

tsbs.title: 3.6 Pentastar left cylinder head (X56)
tsbs.summary: 2012–2013 JKs with misfire codes P0300/P0302/P0304/P0306: check cylinder leakage and replace the left head. Warranty Bulletin D-14-12 extended head coverage to 10 years/150,000 miles.

tsbs.title: Water leaks
tsbs.summary: Bulletins cover cowl trim panel fastener leaks (water on the front floor, 2012–2014), door and windshield-frame gaps, and Freedom Top centre-seal leaks.

timeline.change: JK launch (production from August 2006): 3.8 EGH V6 (202 hp) with a 6-speed manual or 4-speed 42RLE auto; Rubicon has Dana 44s with lockers, 4:1 Rock-Trac and a sway-bar disconnect; the four-door Unlimited is new. First-year trucks drew several recalls (SlashGear), 2007–08 log the most complaints on CarComplaints.com (CarGurus), and Driving Line warns the 3.8 burns oil, leaks intake gaskets and cracks exhaust manifolds
Hill Start Assist standard; Trailer Sway Control available
Easier-folding soft top; Uconnect on MyGig-equipped trucks
Fully redesigned interior with steering-wheel controls, Bluetooth, and available heated seats and leather. Mopar's JK-8 pickup kit for the Unlimited also arrives.

3.6 Pentastar V6 (285 hp, 260 lb-ft) and 5-speed W5A580 automatic replace the 3.8 and the 4-speed. The Pentastar is the engine to have (Quadratec, Driving Line); Driving Line's daily-driver pick is a 2013 or newer
Some Pentastars have faulty left cylinder heads (misfire codes); covered by the X56 extension to 10 years/150,000 miles
Second windshield-washer nozzle returns; one-handed rear-seat fold; Moab edition with AEV bumpers. The millionth JK is built in May 2013.
Clear park and turn lamps; optional 6.5 in Uconnect; Rubicon X edition
Willys Wheeler and Rubicon Hard Rock join the range; Torx tool kit for doors and windshield standard; Alpine audio option
Final year, sold alongside the new JL with 'Wrangler JK' fender decals; Golden Eagle edition. Production ends April 27, 2018.

identify.intro: Twelve years of near-identical bodies, heaps of sticker-pack special editions and plenty of Hemi swaps mean the badge on the hood is only a starting point.

items.head: Real Rubicon
items.body: Dana 44 axles front and rear with Tru-Lok electronic lockers, Rock-Trac transfer case with 4:1 low range, 4.10 gears and an electronic sway-bar disconnect switch. Sport and Sahara trucks have Command-Trac with 2.72:1 low range.

items.head: Axles by trim
items.body: Sport (X) and Sahara have a Dana 30 front and a Dana 44 rear; Quadratec says fewer than a thousand early 2007s got a Dana 35 rear instead (its 2007 spec table lists the Dana 35 for the X). Rubicon has Dana 44s at both ends. A rear locker was optional on X and Sahara for 2007, then on select X models for 2008–2009.

items.head: Engine and year
items.body: 2007–2011 trucks have the 3.8 EGH V6 (4-speed 42RLE auto or 6-speed manual). 2012–2018 trucks have the 3.6 Pentastar (5-speed W5A580 auto or 6-speed manual). 2011 got the new interior a year before the new engine.

items.head: Moab and Rubicon X
items.body: The 2013 Moab has AEV-style bumpers and hood but keeps the 2.72:1 transfer case. The 2014 Rubicon X keeps the full Rubicon drivetrain and adds steel bumpers and a Power Dome hood.

items.head: 2018 JK vs JL
items.body: 2018 JKs sold alongside the new JL carry a 'Wrangler JK' decal on the front fenders.

values.intro: JKs are firmly in used-truck territory. Low miles, Rubicon hardware and a manual gearbox earn the premiums, and tidy late Pentastar trucks outsell early 3.8s.
values.note: Based on 70 two-door JK sales on Bring a Trailer in 2025–26: median about $15.8k, top sale $32,750 for a one-owner, 5k-mile 2015 Rubicon 6-speed.
